Container.Name: MailFlow-backend
Container.Overview: API service for MailFlow, a self-hosted webmail client for existing IMAP/SMTP accounts. Install with MailFlow-frontend. PostgreSQL and Redis are separate prerequisites. The frontend connects internally to backend:3000; no backend host port is published. Configure your own application URL and secrets before starting.
Container.Requires: Create the user-defined Docker network mailflow-network before installation. Both MailFlow containers must join it. Requires reachable PostgreSQL 16+ and Redis 7+ services, a dedicated database/user, and MailFlow-frontend. Preserve the backend network alias and internal port 3000. Start database and Redis before this container.

Config.Name: Session secret
Config.Description: Generate a unique secret with openssl rand -hex 32. Do not reuse an example secret.

Config.Name: Application URL
Config.Description: Full browser-facing URL, including HTTPS and any nonstandard port. Example: https://mail.example.com. Must match Frontend origin.

Config.Name: Frontend origin
Config.Description: Set to the same browser-facing origin as APP_URL, including scheme and port, without a trailing slash.

Config.Name: PostgreSQL host
Config.Description: Database container name on this network, or a reachable database hostname/IP. Not localhost.

Config.Name: PostgreSQL port
Config.Description: Use the database container port for same-network connections; use its published port for a remote host.

Config.Name: Database name
Config.Description: Create this dedicated database before starting MailFlow.

Config.Name: Database user
Config.Description: Existing database role owning the MailFlow database and allowed to create/migrate its tables.

Config.Name: Database password
Config.Description: Password for the configured PostgreSQL role. No password is supplied by this template.

Config.Name: Redis connection URL
Config.Description: Enter your Redis URL, for example redis://redis:6379/0 on the shared network. Include URL-encoded credentials if authentication is enabled.

Config.Name: Credential encryption key
Config.Description: Generate with openssl rand -hex 32 (64 hexadecimal characters). Back up securely; changing or losing it makes stored credentials unreadable.

Config.Name: Internal API port
Config.Description: Keep at 3000: the upstream frontend proxies to backend:3000. This does not publish a host port.

Config.Name: Google OAuth client ID
Config.Description: Optional Google OAuth application client ID. Configure all Google OAuth fields together.

Config.Name: Google OAuth redirect URI
Config.Description: Optional exact registered callback URL: your application origin followed by /oauth/google/callback.

Config.Name: Web push public key
Config.Description: Optional. Generate a matching public/private pair with npx web-push generate-vapid-keys.

Config.Name: Web push private key
Config.Description: Optional private key matching VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY. Keep private and persistent.

Config.Name: Web push contact
Config.Description: Optional. Set with both VAPID keys: your mailto contact address or application URL.

Config.Name: Trusted proxy hops
Config.Description: Leave blank for default behavior. Use 2 only when all frontend access is restricted to your additional trusted reverse proxy; consult upstream guidance.
